subject: DPA clarification: controller/processor roles, logging, retention
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmecorp.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: DPA clarifications & logging/retention items

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap of the items we agreed we'd follow up on related to the DPA and data-handling controls. I pulled these together so we can prioritize and assign owners: 

1) Controller vs. Processor: you asked us to confirm Redwood's role for the use-case discussed (customer-supplied PII processed for product features).
2) Subprocessors: list of current subprocessors and our update cadence (you asked for CSV export).
3) Breach notification: timeline and point of contact (we discussed 72-hour notice vs. 24-hour escalation).
4) Logging & audit: what logs are retained (request/response metadata, redaction practices, access logs), retention defaults, and options for longer retention.
5) Data residency: options for region-specific hosting and confirmation of physical location for logs/backups.
6) Next steps: legal-to-legal call, delivery of doc bundle (DPA v3, SOC 2 summary, subprocessor registry), and a short mutual action plan (MAP).

Attachments: Acme_DPA_questions.xlsx (your annotated questions), redwood-dpa-v3.pdf (current standard), see also the link to our DPA in the HubSpot note.

Ask: could you confirm which items you want prioritized (must-have vs nice-to-have) and whether Tom should lead procurement timelines? Markus from our legal team is cc'd and can take the legal call.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmecorp.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA clarifications & logging/retention items

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from Acme Legal/InfoSec before we schedule the L2L call: 

- Controller/Processor: For our use-case Acme will be the controller of the PII we send. Please confirm Redwood will be classified as a processor under the DPA and abide by controller instructions (no profiling beyond what's needed to serve the API).
- Subprocessors: we need a current exportable list of subprocessors, with their locations and whether they have access to decrypted data. Is that available as a CSV?
- Breach notification: our policy requires initial notification to our security team within 24 hours of discovery and a more detailed report within 72 hours. Can Redwood commit to 24-hour initial notice?
- Logging/audit: can you provide: (a) what request metadata is logged (IP, timestamp, model/route, token counts), (b) whether request/response payloads are logged by default, and (c) options for disabling retention or configuring retention per customer (30/90/365 days).
- Data residency: are logs/archives stored separately from compute? Can we request EU-only storage for backups if we choose EU region?

We'll prioritize controller/processor confirmation, subprocessor CSV, and the breach-notice SLA. Tom will coordinate procurement timelines. Please have Markus or someone on your legal team respond to the controller/processor and breach timeline items.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min legal-to-legal call next week afternoon PST.

Regards,
Elena Rossi
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Acme Corp
elena.rossi@acmecorp.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmecorp.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA clarifications & logging/retention items

Elena — thanks, good questions. High-level answers here so the commercial team can keep momentum; happy to discuss on a legal call and provide formal language or redlines.

1) Controller / Processor: For the typical model-serving scenario you described (Acme supplies PII to Redwood API and instructs processing), Redwood is the Processor. We will accept Controller instructions via the DPA and the Data Processing Addendum reflects that relationship. (I can annotate the specific DPA clauses for clarity.)

2) Subprocessors: attached is a current registry export (redwood-subprocessors.csv). It lists our cloud providers, analytics infra provider, logging vendor, and CDN. Each row includes service name, function, and region. We update this registry monthly and will provide at least 30 days' notice for additions.

3) Breach notification: Our standard timeline is to provide initial notification within 24 hours of detection of a security incident that impacts customer data, followed by a 72-hour preliminary report and a more detailed remediation plan as we investigate. We can add the 24-hour initial notice language into the DPA.

4) Logging & retention: by default we capture request metadata (timestamp, route, model, token counts, client id, request id) and infrastructure access logs. Request/response payloads are NOT retained in plaintext by default for models that process PII — we redact or avoid storing full payloads per customer config. Retention defaults are 30 days for detailed request logs and 7 days for transient caches; we support extended retention options (90/365 days) under dedicated contracts. We can provide an one-page summary of logging options and a sample MAP that shows the choices and estimated cost delta.

5) Data residency: compute and logs can be colocated per region for Private/Dedicated deployments. For hosted customers we can lock storage to a region (e.g., eu-west-1) for backups and logs; full EU-only archival can be arranged via Dedicated or Private setup.

Next steps proposed: 
- I will share annotated DPA excerpts and the subprocessor CSV (attached).
- Vanessa / Tom: please propose two 30-min windows next week for legal-to-legal.
- Vanessa: prepare the MAP & the one-page logging options (we can pull in Product/Infra if needed).

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors.csv.

— Markus Klein
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
